**Finding re-submitted: compliant** — classification unchanged, with the duration point now substantively closed.

What I repaired:

- **Addressed the failed period check with hard evidence.** The quote now anchors on the warranty's own duration language — Vendor warrants "now and throughout the **Term**" (p0041) — and I pulled §4(a) (p0016) to quantify it: the Initial Term is "one (1) year from the Effective Date," auto-renewing in 1-year terms. So the warranty period is a minimum of **twelve (12) months, expressed in years**, which clears the ≥90-day threshold and meets or exceeds the 12-month/90-day preferred benchmark.
- **Added p0016 to the cited paragraphs** so the duration basis is traceable rather than inferred.
- **Kept the reasoning that a numeric period would be a downgrade.** Writing in "ninety (90) days following delivery" would shorten a Term-length warranty, so the absence of a number is a drafting artifact, not a gap.
- **Unchanged conclusions** on the other elements: §13's "Except as expressly set forth herein" carve-out means the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties, and the missing repair/replace/refund sentence is not a material failure because there is no sole/exclusive-remedy language — we keep all remedies at law plus the §4(b) cure-and-terminate right. Adding the model remedy would cap us and give Vendor the election, so it stays unflagged.
- Minor sub-elements (industry-standards rather than documentation conformance; no separate "professional and workmanlike" wording) remain noted in the rationale only.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline and no counterparty comment were proposed.
